full_judgment: 2. The facts, relevant for the purpose of disposal of this Rule are that the pre-emptor-opposite party No. 1, Md Nurul Islam, instituted the Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 27 of 2004 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Charfasion, Bhola for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 stating, inter alia, that the case land appertaining to SA Plot No. 52 and 278 under SA Khatian No. 12 belonged to Ashini Kumar and others. Aswini Kumar sold out some portion of land to Ayesha Khatun. Aswini Kumar further sold out 4 anna 11 gonda 3 kora share to Chandra Kumar Mazi who died leaving behind his 2 (two) sons, Manik Chandra Mazi and Khagandra Chandra Mazi who sold out 61 decimals of land by a registered deed dated 27-3-2003 to the pre-emptor. Haripad Mazi, son of Ashini Kumar Mazi sold out 1.22 acres of land to the pre-emptor by a registered deed dated 9-5-1996. As such, the pre-emptor became co-sharer, owner and possessor of 1.83 acres of land in the disputed Khatian described in the schedule of the pre-emption case. The opposite party No. 2, Abdul Zabbar is one of the co-sharers of the holding who sold out 64 decimals of land on 3-4-2004 to the pre-emptee No. 1, Md Soleman who is the stranger to the case holding without giving any notice to other co-sharers including the pre-emptor. The pre-emptor obtained certified copy on 13-6-2004 of the sale deed and came to know properly as to the transfer of sale and filed the Pre-emption Case No. 27 of 2004.
